title: Geometric irreducibility can be tested on finite separable extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $R$ a commutative $k$-algebra, meaning a commutative ring equipped with a homomorphism $k\to R$. Form tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(r\otimes a)(s\otimes b)=rs\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. The following are equivalent: (1) for every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kL)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]; (2) for every finite separable algebraic field extension $E/k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kE)$ is irreducible. Here finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and irreducible includes nonempty. No finite-generation or reducedness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: Condition (1) implies (2): each finite separable extension is in particular a field extension, so specialize the quantifier in (1).

We record the scalar identifications used below. For fields $k\subseteq E\subseteq F$, put $A_E=R\otimes_kE$ and $A_F=R\otimes_kF$. There is an isomorphism $A_E\otimes_EF\simeq A_F$ sending $(r\otimes e)\otimes f$ to $r\otimes ef$, with inverse $r\otimes f\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes f$. The bilinearity relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] make both formulas well-defined; on pure tensors their composites are identities by $E$-balancing. The multiplication and unit in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] show they are ring maps. The map $A_E\to A_F$ thereby becomes $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with base field $E$, extension $F/E$, and algebra $D=A_E$, followed by the $I=0$ clause of [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]: this map is injective. For $E=k$, use also $R\otimes_kk\simeq R$, $r\otimes c\mapsto cr$, inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$, verified by the same relations.

source.place: Tag 037K proof, scalar-extension maps; tensor bilinearity and faithful-flat injectivity replace the minimal-prime going-down argument.

proof.text:
Assume (2). Take a separable closure $k_s/k$ as in [def-pd-separable-closure], which is separably closed and is the filtered union of its finite separable subextensions. Condition (2) for $E=k$ and the unit isomorphism in Step 2 give irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence $1_R
e0$ by [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime]. Step 2 makes $R	o A=R\otimes_kk_s$ injective, so $1_A
e0$. Thus the nilradical $N_A$ is proper: $1_A^n=1_A
e0$ for every positive integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 037K, (2) implies (3), including nonemptiness of the spectrum.

proof.text: To show $N_A$ is prime, take $x,y\in A$ with $(xy)^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$. By the pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $x$ and $y$ are finite sums of pure tensors. Their finitely many coefficients in $k_s$ lie together in one finite separable subextension $E/k$, by the filtered-union assertion of [def-pd-separable-closure]. Hence $x,y$ are images of elements $x_E,y_E\in A_E$. Step 2 gives injectivity of $A_E\to A$, so $(x_Ey_E)^n=0$. Condition (2) and [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] make $N_{A_E}$ prime, whence $x_E$ or $y_E$ is nilpotent. Its image $x$ or $y$ is nilpotent. Thus $N_A$ is prime and proper, and the same criterion proves $\operatorname{Spec}A$ irreducible. This proves the separable-closure intermediate assertion without assuming finite generation of $R$.

source.place: Tag 037K, (2) implies (3): the finite-subextension argument, expressed using the nilradical criterion Tag 00ES instead of minimal primes.

proof.text: Let $L/k$ now be any field extension. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to $L/k$ and $k_s/k$ to obtain a field $M$ and compatible $k$-embeddings $L\to M$ and $k_s\to M$. Regard $M$ as a $k_s$-algebra via the latter embedding. The nilradical of a field is the zero ideal: a nonzero element is invertible, so cannot have a zero positive power; and a product of two nonzero elements is invertible. It is proper because $1_M\ne0$. Therefore [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] makes $\operatorname{Spec}M$ irreducible. Since $k_s$ is separably closed and Step 4 gives irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, apply [lem-zl-sepclosed-algebras-tensor-irreducible] over $k_s$ to $A$ and $M$. It gives irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{k_s}M)$. Step 2 identifies this ring with $C=R\otimes_kM$.

source.place: Tag 037K, final proof paragraph; Tag 00I7, lemma-separably-closed-irreducible, applied directly over the separable closure.

proof.text: Put $B=R\otimes_kL$. Step 2 applied to $L\subseteq M$ gives an injective unital ring map $v:B\to C$. For each $b\in B$, $v(b)$ is nilpotent if and only if $b$ is nilpotent: $v(b)^n=v(b^n)$, and injectivity detects zero. Thus $N_B=v^{-1}(N_C)$. By Step 5 and [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime], $N_C$ is prime and proper. Its preimage is proper since $v(1)=1\notin N_C$. If $bb\prime\in N_B$, then $v(b)v(b\prime)\in N_C$, so $v(b)$ or $v(b\prime)$ lies in $N_C$, and consequently $b$ or $b\prime$ lies in $N_B$. Thus $N_B$ is prime, and the same criterion gives irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. This holds for every $L/k$, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 037K, final descent from a common overfield, via contraction of the nilradical along the injective scalar-extension map.
